objects.description: Bitset enum of language/parse options for the web demo linter (JSX, TypeScript, or config JSON mode). Used with qljs_web_demo_set_language_options. Values are flag bits, intended to be ORed.
Enum representing diagnostic severity: error or warning. Used in QLJS_Web_Demo_Diagnostic.

Opaque handle to a web demo document containing text, language options, associated config, locale, and produced diagnostics. Created with qljs_web_demo_create_document and destroyed with qljs_web_demo_destroy_document. Not thread-safe for concurrent use of the same instance without external synchronization.

Concrete diagnostic record returned by qljs_web_demo_lint. Contains human-readable message, a short string code, severity, and range offsets measured in UTF-16 code units. Arrays returned by the API are terminated by an item with message == NULL and code == "".

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_create_document
functions.description: Creates a new QLJS_Web_Demo_Document with empty text, no language options, no configuration document, a default locale, and unspecified diagnostics. Use to allocate a document before setting text/options and invoking lint.
requirements: Thread safety: Thread-safe (not async-signal-safe).
Postcondition: Returned pointer is not null.
Caller should later free resources with qljs_web_demo_destroy_document(document).

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_destroy_document
functions.description: Destroys a QLJS_Web_Demo_Document and frees its resources. After this call, the document pointer must not be used.
requirements: Precondition: document was previously returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document().
Precondition: qljs_web_demo_destroy_document(document) has not been called before.
Thread safety: Follow NOTE[QLJS_Web_Demo_Document threads]; do not call functions that accept the same document concurrently without external synchronization.
Postcondition: The document pointer must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_set_text
functions.signature: void qljs_web_demo_set_text(QLJS_Web_Demo_Document* document, const void* text_utf_8, size_t text_byte_count);
functions.description: Sets the document text (UTF-8 bytes) used by qljs_web_demo_lint. The contents are internally copied; modifying the source buffer later has no effect.
requirements: Precondition: document was returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document() and has not been destroyed.
Precondition: text_utf_8 is not null (even if text_byte_count == 0).
Precondition: text_utf_8 points to an array of at least text_byte_count bytes.
Thread safety: Follow NOTE[QLJS_Web_Demo_Document threads]; do not access the same document concurrently without synchronization.
To apply a new config (if set via qljs_web_demo_set_config), you must call qljs_web_demo_lint(document).

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_set_config
functions.description: Associates a configuration document whose text is treated as the quick-lint-js.config for js_document during linting. Pass null to revert to the default config. Language options on the config document are ignored.
requirements: Precondition: js_document was returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document() and has not been destroyed.
Precondition: config_document is null, or it was returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document() and has not been destroyed.
Thread safety: Follow NOTE[QLJS_Web_Demo_Document threads]; do not access the same document concurrently without synchronization.

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_set_language_options
functions.description: Sets parsing/interpretation options for the document (e.g., JSX, TypeScript, or config.json mode) that will affect subsequent linting.
requirements: Precondition: document was returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document() and has not been destroyed.
Precondition: options is a bitwise-or of zero or more QLJS_Language_Options values (0 is permitted).
Thread safety: Follow NOTE[QLJS_Web_Demo_Document threads]; do not access the same document concurrently without synchronization.

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_set_locale
functions.description: Sets the human language used for diagnostics produced by linting this document. If the given locale is unsupported, the default locale (professional US English) is used.
requirements: Precondition: document was returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document() and has not been destroyed.
Precondition: locale is not null and points to a C string.
Thread safety: Follow NOTE[QLJS_Web_Demo_Document threads]; do not access the same document concurrently without synchronization.

functions.name: qljs_web_demo_lint
functions.description: Parses and lints the document’s text using its language options, associated config, and locale, returning a pointer to a diagnostics array terminated by an item with message == null and code == "". The returned pointer remains valid until the next lint on this document or the document is destroyed.
requirements: Precondition: document was returned by qljs_web_demo_create_document() and has not been destroyed.
Precondition: If a config document is associated via qljs_web_demo_set_config, that config document has not been destroyed.
Postcondition: Returned pointer is not null.
Lifetime: The returned diagnostics pointer is valid only until the next qljs_web_demo_lint(document) call or qljs_web_demo_destroy_document(document), whichever comes first.
Thread safety: Follow NOTE[QLJS_Web_Demo_Document threads]; do not access the same document concurrently without synchronization.

functions.name: qljs_list_locales
functions.description: Returns a process-wide, null-terminated array of null-terminated locale strings supported by the library. Repeated calls return the same pointer.
requirements: Thread safety: Thread-safe (not async-signal-safe).
Postcondition: Returned pointer is not null.
Postcondition: The returned array contains at least one non-empty string.
The returned array is null-terminated; each string is null-terminated.

data_types.description: Arbitrary sequence of UTF-8 encoded bytes representing text content. May include valid or invalid Unicode sequences; consumers may interpret as UTF-8 document text.
A C string naming a locale/language tag, typically BCP 47 style (e.g., en, en-US, fr-FR). May be any string; unsupported values should fall back to a default locale.

generators.generator:
import random
import string

# Generator for locale strings suitable for qljs_web_demo_set_locale
# We aim to produce valid, interesting BCP 47-like tags and related variants.
# The fuzzer stub may sometimes pick from qljs_list_locales(); otherwise it uses
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), which our buffer feeds. We therefore emit a single string
# (without embedded NUL) that covers a range of valid locale formats, separated
# by newlines so the harness can slice if it wants. Primary intent: produce a
# single interesting locale per buffer; keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

# Common subtags and components per BCP 47
PRIMARY_LANGS = [
    "en", "fr", "de", "es", "it", "pt", "ru", "zh", "ja", "ko",
    "ar", "hi", "bn", "pa", "ta", "te", "vi", "pl", "nl", "sv",
    "no", "fi", "da", "cs", "sk", "sl", "el", "tr", "he", "uk",
    "ro", "bg", "hr", "sr", "hu", "id", "ms", "th"
]

REGIONS = [
    "US", "GB", "CA", "AU", "NZ", "IE", "IN", "SG", "ZA", "FR",
    "DE", "ES", "IT", "PT", "BR", "MX", "AR", "CL", "JP", "KR",
    "CN", "TW", "HK", "RU", "UA", "PL", "NL", "BE", "SE", "NO",
    "DK", "FI", "CZ", "SK", "SI", "GR", "TR", "IL", "RO", "BG",
    "HR", "RS", "HU", "ID", "MY", "TH", "VN"
]

SCRIPTS = [
    "Latn", "Cyrl", "Grek", "Arab", "Hebr", "Hant", "Hans", "Kana", "Hira",
    "Deva", "Thai", "Cyril",  # include a slightly off one to be unsupported yet valid-looking
]

# Unicode extension keys and common values (u- extensions)
U_KEYS = ["ca", "nu", "kk", "co", "hc", "ks"]
U_VALUES = {
    "ca": ["buddhist", "chinese", "coptic", "ethiopic", "gregory", "hebrew", "islamic", "iso8601"],
    "nu": ["arab", "arabext", "bali", "beng", "deva", "fullwide", "gujr", "guru", "hanidec", "khmr", "knda", "laoo", "latn", "mlym", "mymr", "olck", "orya", "tamldec", "telu", "thai", "tibt"],
    "kk": ["calendar", "collation"],
    "co": ["phonebk", "pinyin", "stroke", "search"],
    "hc": ["h11", "h12", "h23", "h24"],
    "ks": ["level1", "level2", "level3", "identic"]
}

# Transform extension (t-) pieces
T_LANGS = PRIMARY_LANGS
T_REGIONS = REGIONS

# Private use segments (x-)
PRIVATE_SEGMENTS = [
    "foo", "bar", "baz", "test", "x1", "x2", "alpha", "beta", "gamma"
]

# Variants examples (not exhaustive)
VARIANTS = [
    "fonipa", "polyton", "scouse", "valencia", "POSIX", "rozaj", "biske", "nedis"
]

# Likely supported locales to increase chance of matching qljs_list_locales()
LIKELY_SUPPORTED = [
    "en", "en-US", "en-GB", "fr", "fr-FR", "de", "de-DE", "es", "es-ES",
    "pt-BR", "pt-PT", "it-IT", "ja-JP", "ko-KR", "zh-CN", "zh-TW"
]

MAX_LEN = 1024  # stay well under 4096


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _maybe(rng, p):
    return rng.random() < p


def _rand_token(rng, min_len=1, max_len=8, alphabet=string.ascii_letters + string.digits):
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def build_bcp47_like(rng):
    parts = []

    # 1) Primary language
    if _maybe(rng, 0.85):
        lang = _rand_choice(rng, PRIMARY_LANGS)
    else:
        # Occasionally generate a 2-3 letter made-up language subtag
        lang = _rand_token(rng, 2, 3, string.ascii_lowercase)
    parts.append(lang)

    # 2) Optional script
    if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, SCRIPTS))

    # 3) Optional region
    if _maybe(rng, 0.6):
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, REGIONS))

    # 4) 0-2 variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, VARIANTS))

    tag = '-'.join(parts)

    # 5) Optional Unicode extension (-u- key[-type]*)
    if _maybe(rng, 0.5):
        u_parts = ["u"]
        # 1-3 keys
        keys = rng.sample(U_KEYS, rng.randint(1, min(3, len(U_KEYS))))
        for k in keys:
            u_parts.append(k)
            vals = U_VALUES.get(k, [])
            if vals and _maybe(rng, 0.8):
                # 1 value, occasionally 2
                vcount = 1 if not _maybe(rng, 0.2) else 2
                for _ in range(vcount):
                    u_parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, vals))
        tag += '-' + '-'.join(u_parts)

    # 6) Optional transform extension (-t- ...)
    if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
        t_parts = ["t", _rand_choice(rng, T_LANGS)]
        if _maybe(rng, 0.5):
            t_parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, T_REGIONS))
        tag += '-' + '-'.join(t_parts)

    # 7) Optional private use (-x- ...)
    if _maybe(rng, 0.4):
        priv_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
        priv = ['x'] + [ _rand_choice(rng, PRIVATE_SEGMENTS) for _ in range(priv_count) ]
        tag += '-' + '-'.join(priv)

    return tag


def build_interesting_locale(rng):
    # Mix between known-likely supported, strict BCP47-like, and edge-y cases.
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.35:
        return _rand_choice(rng, LIKELY_SUPPORTED)
    elif roll < 0.8:
        return build_bcp47_like(rng)
    else:
        # Edge but valid C-strings: empty, simple, uppercase, numeric variants, long chains
        choices = []
        choices.append("en")
        choices.append("en-us")  # lowercase region
        choices.append("EN-US")  # uppercase everything
        choices.append("sr-Cyrl-RS")
        choices.append("zh-Hant-TW")
        choices.append("sl-rozaj-biske")
        # Long but reasonable chain (still < MAX_LEN)
        long_chain = "en-Latn-US" + "-x-" + "-".join([_rand_token(rng, 1, 6) for _ in range(10)])
        choices.append(long_chain)
        return _rand_choice(rng, choices)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many locales to emit. Although the stub pulls a single string,
    # providing multiple separated by newlines can be useful when the harness
    # slices inputs; we still keep overall size small and each line a valid tag.
    count = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.randint(2, 6)

    locales = []
    for _ in range(count):
        tag = build_interesting_locale(rng)
        locales.append(tag)

    payload = "\n".join(locales)
    # Ensure we don't exceed limits and avoid NUL bytes.
    payload = payload[:MAX_LEN]

    # Return bytes without NUL; API expects C string but the fuzzer provides it.
    return payload.encode('utf-8')
